div.head: I Em 1
div.ab: Ðæt is æres[t] þæt hi budon, þæt þa halgan hadas, þe Godes folc læron sculon lifes bisne, ðæt hi heora clænnesse healdan be heora hade, swa werhades swa wifhades, swa hwaðer swa hit sy. ⁊ gif hi swa ne don, þonne syn hi þæs wyrðe þe on ðam canone cweð, and þæt hi þolian worldæhta ⁊ gehalgodre legerstowe, buton hi gebetan.

Ðæt is ærest, ðæt ða halgan hadas, ðe Godes folc læron scylan lyfes bysne, ðæt hi heora clænnesse healdan be heora hade, swa werhades swa wifhades, swa hweðer hit sy. Gif hy swa ne don, þonne syn hy ðæs wyrðe ðe on ðam canone cwæð: ðæt is, ðæt hy ðolian woroldæhta ⁊ gehalgodre legerstowe, buton hy gebetan.

Þæt is ærest, þæt ða halgan hadas, ðe Godes folc læran scylan lifes bysne, þæt hy heora clænnesse heoldan be heora hade, swa werhades swa wifhades, swæðer hit sy. Gif hy swa ne don, ðonne syn hy ðæs wyrðe ðe on ðam canone cwæð: þæt is, þæt hy ðolian woroldæhta ⁊ gehalgodre legerstowe, buton hy gebetan.

In primis est, ut sanctis ordinibus euecti, qui plebem Dei docere debent lumen uite, castitatem teneant secundum ordinem suum, sic ƿerhades sic ƿifhades, sit alterutrum sit. Alioquin sint eius digni, quod in canone est dictum: hoc est, ut perdant secularem pecuniam et sanctificata legerstoƿa (id est positionis loca), si non conuertantur et emendent.

[Be gehadeda manna clænnisse.] Ðæt is æres[t] þæt hi budon, þæt þa halgan hadas þe Godes folc læron sculon lifes bisne, ðæt hi heora clænnesse healdan be heora hade, swa werhades swa wifhades, swa hwaðer swa hit sy. ⁊ gif hi swa ne don, þonne syn hi þæs wyrðe þe on ðam canone cweð, and þæt hi þolian worldæhta ⁊ gehalgodre legerstowe, buton hi gebetan.

Ðæt is ærest þæt hi budon: þæt þa halgan hadas þe Godes folc læron sculon lifes bisne, ðæt hi heora clænnesse healdan be heora hade, swa werhades swa wifhades, swa hwaðer swa hit sy. And gif hi swa ne don, þonne syn hi þæs wyrðe þe on ðam canone cweð, and þæt hi þolian worldæhta and gehalgodre legerstowe buton hi gebetan.

(Über Keuschheit der Geistlichen. Ld). Nämlich erstens (dass sie geboten D), dass die kirchlich geweihten Personen, welche Gottes Volk belehren sollen durch Beispiel [ihres] Lebens, dass sie ihre Keuschheit ihrem Stande gemäss bewahren, sowohl vom männlichen Geschlecht wie vom weiblichen, von welchem es auch sei. Und wenn sie nicht so handeln, dann seien sie des [Strafmasses] theilhaftig, wie es im Kanon heisst, und (nämlich H B Qu.) dass sie der weltlichen Güter [Temporalien] und geweihten Grabesstätte verlustig gehen, es sei denn, sie thun Busse.

(On the chastity of the clergy. Ld) Namely, first (that they commanded, D), that the ecclesiastically consecrated persons who are to teach God's people by the example of [their] life, that they keep their chastity in accordance with their order, whether of the male sex or the female, whichever it may be. And if they do not do so, then let them incur the [penalty] as it says in the canon, and (namely, H B Qu.) that they lose their worldly goods [temporalities] and a consecrated burial-place, unless they make amends.

This is their first injunction: that those in holy orders whose duty it is to teach God's people by the example of their life should observe the celibacy befitting their estate, whether they be men or women. If they fail to do so, they shall incur that which is ordained in the canon, and they shall forfeit their worldly possessions and burial in consecrated ground, unless they make amends.

This was the first of their decrees: that those in holy orders who must teach God’s people using their own life as an example are to embrace celibacy in the manner appropriate to their order, whether it is for men or women. And if they do not do so, let them suffer that which is decreed in the canon, and let them forfeit all their worldly property and burial in consecrated ground unless they repent.

note.seg: Be gehadeda³ manna clænnisse Rubrik Ld
Be gehadeda³ manna clænnisse rubric in Ld
written above it in the 16th cent.: after B
gehadeda statt -dra kann Ld's Druckfehler sein: Lambarde druckte Endungen öfter nicht genau, was ich ferner nicht notiere
gehadeda instead of -dra may be a misprint of Ld's: Lambarde often printed endings inaccurately, which I do not record further
Die Worte þæt hi budon können wohl original (also von der anderen Hss.-Klasse fortgelassen) sein; entsprechend beginnt EGu 1
The words þæt hi budon may well be original (and so omitted by the other class of MSS); EGu 1 begins correspondingly
Q nimmt bysne, das er nur ungefähr übersetzt, als Accusativ. Allein ein ‘Lebensbeispiel’ wird nicht gelehrt, sondern gegeben.—Derselbe Gedanke u. 5³
Q takes bysne, which he translates only approximately, as an accusative. But an ‘example of life’ is not taught but given.—The same idea below 5³

Offenbar wird der Cölibat (s. d. Gl 1—f) hier nicht etwa auf Prälaten oder Stiftsgeistliche beschränkt. Ebenso unter Eadgar und Æthelred. Doch wird er hier allein bei Verlust der Pfründe und christlichen Grabes (s. d. Gl 2a) geboten

Clearly celibacy (see that word in Gl 1—f) is not here restricted, say, to prelates or canons. Likewise under Eadgar and Æthelred. Here, however, it is enjoined only on pain of loss of the benefice and of Christian burial (see that word in Gl 2a)

Vgl. Gl Kanones 10a; Kirchenstaatsrecht 22—24h. Mir scheint, gegen Thorpe und Schmid, D's Lesung richtig, wie auch EGu 3 neben die kanonische Strafe die weltliche stellt, die in jenem Kanon nicht enthalten gewesen sein kann. Weltliche Gewalt zwingt den Priester, dem Bischofe zu gehorchen, auch IV Eg 1, 8

Cf. Gl Kanones 10a; Kirchenstaatsrecht 22—24h. To me, against Thorpe and Schmid, D's reading seems correct, just as EGu 3 also sets beside the canonical penalty the secular one, which cannot have been contained in that canon. Secular power compels the priest to obey the bishop also in IV Eg 1, 8
Amtsverlust versteht Taranger. Unkeuschheit mindert die Grabesehre auch V Atr 9, 1; vgl. Gl Grab 2a B
Taranger understands loss of office. Unchastity diminishes the honour of burial also in V Atr 9, 1; cf. Gl Grab 2a B
Q translates Qui plebem Dei docere debent lumen vitae. For other examples of the use of læran with a double acc. see Toller, Suppl. p. 601, s.v. iv (2 β), v (3). My translation follows Liebermann’s.

The reading of D, as against H and B, is preferred by Liebermann who points out that what follows would not be prescribed by the canon law. It may be suggested that the presence of þæt before hi in D is ungrammatical, and points to an (imperfect) correction.
